sources.locator: Abstract; Methodology: Study subject and Study sites
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0); article copyright notice and PLOS licensing policy
sources.scope: Playback and phonotaxis study of wild and captive male M. aurantiaca from Mangabe, Mitsinjo Captive Breeding Centre and Chester Zoo; results do not estimate species-wide behaviour or reintroduction outcomes.
sources.rightsHolder: The authors, who retain copyright under the PLOS article license.

claims.text: In this experiment, wild males showed similar phonotaxis responses to calls from wild and captive conspecifics, while Chester Zoo males responded more strongly to calls from their separately housed Chester Zoo conspecific group.
claims.placeTimeScope: Sampled wild calls at Mangabe, Madagascar, and captive calls at Mitsinjo, Madagascar, and Chester Zoo, United Kingdom; the paper was published in 2017.
claims.lifeStatus: The study directly compared wild and captive male frogs; reported responses apply to the sampled animals and test conditions.

gaps: This playback experiment does not establish responses across all wild populations, life stages or field settings, and it does not measure reintroduction success.

reasons: Only one bounded behavioural study has been assessed; six facets remain unassessed.

claims.text: The authors reported that the assembled axolotl genome lacks Pax3, and that mutation of its Pax7 paralogue produced a phenotype similar to Pax3- or Pax7-mutant mice; the genomic sample came from one three-year-old d/d adult male.
claims.locator: Abstract; Methods, genomic DNA preparation; Results, Reduced Pax-family complement
claims.placeTimeScope: A single laboratory-bred d/d male supplied genomic DNA; the 2018 article presents comparative genomic and gene-editing results, not a population survey.
claims.lifeStatus: The source concerns laboratory material and experimental mutants; it does not establish the frequency of these genomic traits across wild populations.

gaps: One genome assembly and associated experiments do not resolve genomic variation across the species, the evolutionary timing of the reported changes, or broader evolutionary history.

reasons: Only a bounded evolutionary-genomics study has been assessed; six facets remain unassessed.

sources.title: Bina Perl et al. (2017), Natural history and conservation of the rediscovered Hula painted frog, Latonia nigriventer
sources.version: Contributions to Zoology 86(1), 11–37; final version published 2017
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the Naturalis item record for the final version
sources.scope: Multi-disciplinary natural-history and immunity surveys of L. nigriventer in the Hula Valley; abstract-level claims here retain the paper's local survey and publication scope.
sources.rightsHolder: The authors, as identified by the Naturalis item record.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Final article version as released under CC BY 4.0 in the Naturalis record; claims here paraphrase the abstract and no figures or supplementary files are reused.
sources.attribution: Bina Perl RG, Gafny S, Malka Y, Renan S, Woodhams DC, Rollins-Smith L, et al. (2017). Natural history and conservation of the rediscovered Hula painted frog, Latonia nigriventer. Contributions to Zoology 86(1): 11–37. https://doi.org/10.1163/18759866-08601002. Claims here are paraphrased.

claims.text: The authors describe L. nigriventer tadpole morphology as similar to that of its sister group Discoglossus.
claims.placeTimeScope: Comparative tadpole observations reported in the 2017 Hula Valley natural-history paper; the claim does not describe all morphology or all stages.
claims.lifeStatus: The observation concerns tadpoles; adult morphology and other developmental stages are not inferred.

gaps: The abstract supplies a comparative summary rather than a complete diagnosis or quantitative account of morphological variation.

claims.text: The authors characterize breeding phenology as opportunistic and report adults' extended annual presence in aquatic habitat.
claims.placeTimeScope: Natural-history surveys summarized in the 2017 paper; conclusions are limited to the authors' study period and Hula Valley field context.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild adult and tadpole observations; exact breeding dates or year-round population occupancy are not inferred beyond the source summary.

gaps: The abstract does not establish precise breeding dates, age at maturity, longevity, survival or full seasonal variation.

claims.text: The surveys describe L. nigriventer as localized and elusive; they detected Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis in the region and on sampled frogs but observed no signs of chytridiomycosis in this species.
claims.placeTimeScope: Hula Valley surveys summarized in the 2017 publication; the pathogen observation is restricted to that study's sampled place, time and frogs.
claims.lifeStatus: Wild survey observations; pathogen detection is not interpreted as clinical disease or a current population-wide condition.

gaps: The abstract does not provide a complete distribution model, prevalence estimate, long-term trend or current disease assessment.

reasons: The selected primary study provides only bounded local evidence for morphology, life history and ecology; four facets remain unassessed.
No systematic current literature search or complete comparison with the COL26.8 concept has been completed.
No independent expert review has been completed.
